newsitem.title: GERMANY: German draft share law--shareholder meeting,shares.
newsitem.headline: German draft share law--shareholder meeting,shares.

text.p: The German Justice Ministry on Tuesday released details of a new draft share law. The following is a summary of the sections of the draft referring to shareholder meetings and shares.

The new draft makes some changes to current laws which give banks the right to exercise votes as they see fit on behalf of shareholders who have deposited shares at the bank unless they have express instructions to the contrary from the shareholder.
The summary was provided by the ministry in German and translated by Reuters.
* The allocation of proxy votes by shareholders is to be made easier by means of electronic banking.

* The exercise of proxy votes by credit institutions is to be more oriented to the interests of the shareholders. The credit institution must name a member of its management whose responsibility it is to ensure that the institution abides by the statutory requirements.
* Credit institutions and companies must make shareholders aware of alternative means of exercising their voting rights (via transfer of the proxy to someone else or to a shareholder group).

* The requirements of the credit institution to inform holders of deposit accounts in the case of a conflict of interests is increased. Customers must be informed if a member of staff at the credit institution is in the supervisory board of the company concerned and/or if a stake is held in the company.
* A call for a special study by a certain quorum of shareholders is to be made possible.

* The shareholder meeting is to be specifically empowered to set itself standing orders on the conduct of a shareholder meeting. Through this the possibility of streamlining and revitalising the shareholder meeting should be made possible.

* Multiple voting rights will no longer be allowed. Even existing multiple voting rights will expire after five years. If the shareholder has paid for these rights then the procedure for withdrawal of this is laid down in paragraph five section two of the income tax laws, which calls for appropriate compensation.
* Maximum voting rights are no longer permitted. Existing restrictions expire after two years.
* In the case of cross-shareholdings one company is not allowed to exercise of the voting rights in the other company when it comes to the election of supervisory board members.

* Restrictions governing the buyback of a company's shares are further relaxed in line with EU directives. This should allow the company more flexibility and promote increased price speculation on the German bourse. Dangers of misuse will be defined by law.
* The granting of stock options as to managers as part of their salary package is to be made easier. Self-service is to be ruled out. All details must be approved by the shareholder meeting.
